title: Project: a bounded async pipeline with cancellation
body: This project builds a reusable producer/worker pipeline on `System.Threading.Channels`. `BoundedPipeline.RunAsync` writes items into a bounded channel, starts a fixed number of workers that read and process them, and returns the sum of their results. It combines stages 11 and 12: bounded capacity for backpressure, cooperative cancellation and `Task.WhenAll` for completion.

The tests check behaviour rather than implementation: every result is summed, no more than `workers` items run at once, the producer stops early when the channel is full (backpressure), cancellation surfaces as `OperationCanceledException`, and bad arguments fail before any work starts.

Concurrency tests need care to stay deterministic. The backpressure test blocks the worker on a `TaskCompletionSource` and asserts a range rather than an exact count; the concurrency test records the peak with `Interlocked.CompareExchange`. `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` (xUnit v3) cancels tests that hang when the run is aborted.

The base version has a lifetime flaw: if one worker throws, the other workers and the producer keep waiting for items or space, so `RunAsync` can hang and work outlives the failed call. The validator also injects a different bug (ignoring the capacity) to show the backpressure test catches it.

Practice: make a worker failure cancel the whole run. Own a linked `CancellationTokenSource` for the duration of `RunAsync`, cancel it when a worker fails, wait for every task to finish, and rethrow the original exception rather than a sibling's cancellation. Any task that exits by exception, including a worker whose own timeout cancels it and a source that throws mid-iteration, must cancel the run. The answer's new tests prove no worker is still running when `RunAsync` completes and that neither case hangs.
This ownership rule (work started by a call finishes, or is cancelled, before the call returns) is what prevents leaked tasks, captured state and unobserved exceptions in long-running services.
projectInstructions: Run dotnet test from the solution folder. Practice: make a worker failure cancel the producer and other workers, wait for them all, and rethrow the original exception.

projectChecks.name: start: injected capacity bug is caught

challenge: Make a worker failure cancel the whole run, wait for every task and rethrow the original exception; prove no worker outlives RunAsync.
question: In the base pipeline, what can happen when one worker throws?
correct: Other workers and the producer keep waiting, so the call can hang and work outlives it
wrong: The channel automatically cancels every other worker
The exception is swallowed and the sum is returned
reasoning: Nothing links the failure to the others. Owning a linked CancellationTokenSource lets the failure stop all work before the call returns.
